en.title: Benissa, Moraira and Fanadix
en.excerpt: A 30.04 km marathon-training run with sea views, long climbs, cyclists everywhere and the best home-made paella waiting afterwards.
en.body:
This was supposed to be a steady long run for marathon training. Around Benissa, that meant accepting the hills, taking the climbs calmly and enjoying the descents. The sun was on my back, the roads were good, and there were cyclists everywhere. Other runners? Somehow, I did not see a single one.

The run took me through Benissa, Moraira and Fanadix. The activity export records 30.04 km, with an average pace of approximately 4:43/km. It was a proper long run, and a very enjoyable one.

## From Benissa to Moraira

I started in Benissa and headed towards Moraira. There were good stretches beside the road, sea views along the way and plenty of climbing still to come. Moraira itself was beautiful, the sort of place that makes a training run feel like a good way to explore.

![Moraira and El Portet bay seen from Cap d'Or](/assets/uploads/benissa-moraira-fanadix/moraira-seafront.jpg "Moraira and El Portet bay, seen from Cap d'Or.")

Photo: [Luciamaldofer / Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bah%C3%ADa_de_Moraira.jpg), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Resized.

After Moraira, the route continued onwards and upwards. There were some big climbs and descents, so I tried to keep the uphill effort relaxed. The sunshine did its best to make that harder than it sounded.

![A winding paved road beside stone walls and houses near Benissa](/assets/uploads/benissa-moraira-fanadix/benissa-quiet-road.jpg "Good asphalt, with another bend and climb ahead.")

## A place that cyclists seem to know about

The number of bikes was hard to miss. I kept seeing cyclists, while apparently being the only person who had decided to do the whole thing on foot. From what I saw, this area seemed especially popular for cycling trips.

For running, I liked the asphalt and the variety. One stretch could be beside the sea, the next heading back into the hills. Some sections were comfortable to run along, but this was still a roadside run, with cars and bends that needed my attention.

I would keep headphones quiet enough to hear what was going on around me. Good road surfaces do not remove the need to be careful beside traffic.

![A cycling climb sign for Puerto Pedramala beside a winding road](/assets/uploads/benissa-moraira-fanadix/pedramala-climb.jpg "The Puerto Pedramala sign: the cyclists were clearly onto something.")

## A drink stop, then more hills

Around halfway, I stopped at a shop for a quick drink before carrying on. A simple break, but a useful one with more climbing ahead.

![A roadside drink break with running shoes in the foreground and a passing cyclist](/assets/uploads/benissa-moraira-fanadix/roadside-drink-stop.jpg "A roadside drink break, with another cyclist passing by.")

Looking back at the GPX, there is an uphill stretch near the start, followed by longer climbs around kilometres 11 to 13, 20 to 22 and 24 to 27. Those positions are approximate and measured along the GPX line. The last part of the route heads downhill again.

![Elevation profile showing the climbs and descents along the supplied route](/assets/uploads/benissa-moraira-fanadix/elevation-profile.svg "Elevation from the supplied GPX; kilometre positions are approximate.")

## The best part might have been afterwards

After the run, I sat down to the best paella I have ever eaten, prepared by my friend. That was a fairly convincing argument for staying a little longer.

![A large seafood paella ready to eat after the run](/assets/uploads/benissa-moraira-fanadix/post-run-paella.jpg "My favourite kind of finish line: paella.")

## Would I come back?

I already have. I have travelled here to run twice, and I would not rule out another visit.

The scenery was very good, both beside the sea and up in the hills. It did not quite have the wow factor of my [Nice to Monaco run](/journal/nice-to-monaco/), but it came close. Good asphalt, a varied route and plenty to look at made the effort worthwhile.

For a beginner, the climbs could make a long outing here fairly demanding. Shorter out-and-back runs, with some walking on the uphill sections, would be a way to keep it manageable. For my marathon training, the hills were part of the appeal, as long as I took them at my own effort.
